arms_note: Two published spiral-arm FITS, not pictures, drawn in different styles because they disagree: the maser fit (Reid et al. 2019) covers mainly the l < 180 deg side of the Sun, the Cepheid fit (Drimmel et al. 2024) the l > 180 deg side, and at the Sun's azimuth their Local/Orion arms are 0.93 kpc apart. Each is drawn only where it was fitted. width_kpc (Reid) is the arm width of Table 2 as SpiralMap transcribes it; SpiralMap draws the band edges at (R_kink +- width/2) exp(-(beta - beta_kink) tan psi).

format: Milky Way galaxy layer v1 (CONTRACT.md section 8)

frame.axes: x from the Sun towards the Galactic centre (the Sun at x = -8.122 kpc), y towards Galactic longitude 90 deg (the direction of the Sun's rotation), z towards the North Galactic Pole; right-handed. The disc rotates clockwise seen from +z.
frame.name: astropy Galactocentric v4.0
refs: Galactic-centre direction (galcen_coord; Galactic l = b = 0 to 0.001 deg) at ICRS RA 266.4051, Dec -28.936175 deg: 2004ApJ...616..872R
frame.to_icrs_note: 4x4 row-major, column vectors: [x_icrs, y_icrs, z_icrs, 1] = to_icrs . [x_gc, y_gc, z_gc, 1], kpc in and out. The upper-left 3x3 is a rotation (orthonormal), so the inverse is x_gc = R^T (x_icrs - t). ICRS here is heliocentric: astropy puts it at the solar-system barycentre, < 1e-10 kpc from the Sun.

fields.dist_err_kpc: [minus, plus] error, kpc, from the catalogued distance-modulus errors
fields.galaxy_confirmed: LVDB confirmed_galaxy (dark-matter dominated galaxy confirmed); false = could still be a star cluster
fields.pa_deg: position angle on the sky, degrees east of north
fields.ref: the paper the distance comes from (author year (ADS bibcode))

lvdb_selection.globulars: LVDB v1.1.1 gc_harris (all confirmed) + gc_mw_new with confirmed_real = 1
lvdb_selection.satellites: LVDB v1.1.1 dwarf_mw with confirmed_real = 1 (host "lmc" = a satellite of the LMC)

components.angle_note: bar_angle = -25 deg "orientation of the bar w.r.t. the Sun" in the script (Sun at x = -8.2 kpc there); its major axis points to -25 / 155 deg, the near end on the l > 0 side (a point 3 kpc out along it lies at l = +13.2 deg). The script says the model fits the central ~5 kpc and is "not very realistic further out".
components.model: Portail et al. (2017) analytic approximation, Sormani et al. 2022; Agama py/example_mw_bar_potential.py makeBarDensity()
components.name: bar (X-shaped short bar + two long bars)
components.sigma: rho integrated over z by Gauss-Legendre quadrature (0-8 kpc, x2)

model.not_included: McMillan's axisymmetric bulge and HI / H2 gas discs, the Sormani model's own disc and central mass concentration, and every dark-matter halo: the image is the two stellar discs plus the bar only.
model.orientation: Face-on from the North Galactic Pole, like the young-star maps: column c, row r (row 0 = top) covers x = x0 + (c + 0.5)(x1 - x0)/W, y = y1 - (r + 0.5)(y1 - y0)/H; +x right towards the Galactic centre from the Sun, +y up towards l = 90 deg.
model.quantity: stellar surface density Sigma, Msun per kpc^2 (grayscale code, see stretch)
refs: Portail et al. (2017) bar, analytic approximation of Sormani et al. 2022 (MNRAS Letters/514/L5) (Agama py/example_mw_bar_potential.py)

stretch.formula: code = round(255 * clip((log10 Sigma - log10 black) / (log10 white - log10 black), 0, 1))
stretch.inverse: Sigma = black * (white / black) ** (code / 255)   (code 0 means Sigma <= black)
stretch.why: white is the map maximum and black the disc surface density at R = 20 kpc, each rounded up to 2 significant digits, so the disc fades to zero just inside the square

vertical_profiles.bar_x_shaped: z0 of the X-shaped bar (Coleman et al. 2020 form): 1/cosh(a^m) with a built from |x|/x0, |y|/y0, |z|/z0
vertical_profiles.thick: exp(-|z| / h): Agama Disk with a positive scaleHeight
vertical_profiles.thin: exp(-|z| / h): Agama Disk with a positive scaleHeight

model.what: A MODEL, not an image: the face-on stellar surface density of two published mass models added together - the McMillan (2017) thin and thick discs and the Portail et al. (2017) bar in the analytic form of Sormani et al. (2022). Nothing here was photographed; it shows where the models put the stars.

young.licence_note: Gaia-derived maps, included in SpiralMap 0.27 with the authors' permission; ESA/Gaia/DPAC data terms (CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO, non-commercial) are taken to apply.
young.orientation: Face-on, seen from the North Galactic Pole (+z). Column c (0 = left) and row r (0 = top) of the W x H image cover x = x0 + (c + 0.5)(x1 - x0)/W and y = y1 - (r + 0.5)(y1 - y0)/H, with extent_kpc = [x0, x1, y0, y1] in this frame: +x (right) towards the Galactic centre, +y (up) towards l = 90 deg. Each pixel centre is one node of the published grid (heliocentric, 0.1 kpc). In three.js a PlaneGeometry(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) centred on the extent, lying in the x-y plane, with its default UVs and texture.flipY = true shows it the right way round.
young.orientation_source: SpiralMap plots the grids as contourf(x, y, grid.T), i.e. grid[ix, iy] with x heliocentric towards the Galactic centre (x_gc = x_hc + x_sun) and y towards l = 90 deg. verify_galaxy.py confirms it on the shipped PNGs: young open clusters (UCC, younger than 50 Myr) sit on about twice the mean overdensity in this orientation than in any of the other 7 flips and transposes.
young.plane: The grids are projections onto the Galactic plane b = 0 through the Sun. That plane lies 5.4 to 36.2 pc above z = 0 across the map; z_kpc places the image flat at the Sun's height. Placing the grid nodes exactly with astropy instead of on the flat rectangle moves none of them by more than 26 micro-kpc.
young.what: How much young stars crowd together compared with their smooth large-scale density (overdensity, dimensionless: 0 = average, > 0 more, < 0 fewer), measured from Gaia parallaxes on 0.1 kpc cells within 6 kpc of the Sun. The maps are published data products (kernel-smoothed), not star lists. Gaia measures young stars well only to about 4 kpc: beyond that most cells hold no data and are transparent.
